The below is ⟦0⟧ player suggested strategies for ⟦1⟧. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.

In a starting scenario Ecuador is not a very powerful country. Being surrounded by powerful neighbors, especially at a brink of war with Peru, it risks losing its provinces or getting annexed. With a small population and a small underequipped force, a tiny air force of 12 P-6 planes and a democratic government it is unlikely to unlock its potential for expansion. In this case, becoming Gran Colombia.

Politically wise, it would be preferable to become Fascist, or becoming Communist. As it will serve to justify goals much quicker on your northern neighbor Colombia along with Panama and Venezuela. Additionally with their perks, it will solve up manpower issues if given time. And, make sure to rush down for industrial focus, as having more factories, civilian or military, will certainly help. The best option to improve your army performance against Peru is to build land forts and just in case coastal forts (should Peru naval invade around the port). And train as much infantry to set them in the Peruvian border, and leave a small defensive infantry brigade of 4 battalions to defend the capital, and the Galapagos island. As time passes by and the tensions rise, consider upgrading the army with few support battalions, and research Marine troops. Because of the Jungle terrain that both countries share, it will be beneficial for Ecuador to gain the upper hand. Request license for the P-6 planes from the US, or from another country for a fighter plane depending on the players choice, as researching one will take time as well. For extra air defense, research and build anti aircraft to prevent the enemy aircraft gain superiority on your airspace. Be sure to built railways to connect supply hub to the frontline.

At a certain point, while preparing the defenses, Peru will declare war on you without warning. Both nations gain the Amazonian War buff, that unfortunately, cannot join a faction, but gain infantry buffs, and a 2% recruitable population. Fortunately, in Ecuador's case, it will gain additional 5 infantry brigades that spawn in the border with Peru which will help to turn the tide. You will stay in a defensive position on the border with Peru because the Peruvian AI will endlessly attack your line. After a period of time the Peruvians will have lost most of its manpower and equipment attacking your line and they won't be able to break through. When you see that the Peruvians are low on equipment then you can start to push and invade their lands without too many problems. Again though the key is to be entrenched and let their army grind away on your front line until their troops are weakened. Once this happens only then should you put your army on the offensive. It may be worthwhile to consider building more land forts and infrastructure on the border before the war to make things easier on your army when the Peruvian AI starts to grind away on you. Then when you capitulate them, you will just annex them.

After the war is finished in your favor, the road for expansion has been opened. What remains to be done is to take the war at their land, one nation at a time. And, hopefully neither of them has joined a bigger faction (Allies or Axis, respectively) or a domestic faction such as the Mexican led Bolivarian alliance (should they turn communist or fascist)

Colombia is the next nation for the challenge. Although similarly stronger as Peru, it possesses more strength than the latter, albeit and a bigger navy. But less of a chance for naval invasion. And, the sole option remains on continuing the land warfare with them. Their terrain is a mix of Jungles and Mountains, thus it is advised to deploy Mountaineer troops, not to forget to adjust support battalions on their way. Last but not least, be sure to have taken special forces doctrines for Marines and Mountaineers to increase your favors in your odds. Same starting strategy to be applied just like with the Peruvian War beforehand. Push the troops on the offensive line after they have been worn out from their attack. In the meantime, if Colombia is halfway done for capitulation, be sure to justify on Panama. It paints as an easy target, and fortunately the capital city is close to the Colombian border, making it quick to capitulate. Be quick to seize them first, as it will fall randomly in the hands of the Mexican forces if they go for the Central American focus

Venezuela has a larger army and will put up more of a fight. It is likely to join a faction, or has already joined one, if the tensions are high and more troops will fill the frontlines. Be sure to justify on them quickly, and bring more of the inherited arsenal on force display against them. The Colombian prized navy, air force, the special forces and by this point have researched tanks. The scenario is similar with Colombia in terms of terrain, and it is the right time to utilize naval invasions, as your army in the frontline pin down the bordering troops. Annex them immediately, and sooner or later, you will form Gran Colombia
